rationale: Lycopolitan reflex of ⲡⲁϩⲣⲉ 'medicine, drug.' Recurs three times on this page (lines 1, 2) as the structuring image of the chapter's parable. Standard Coptic medical lexeme.
Lycopolitan reflex of ⲡϣⲱⲛⲉ 'the sick.' Confirmed by collocation 'medicines that the sick eat' and parallel ⲡⲓⲣⲱⲙⲉ ⲉⲧϣⲱⲛⲉ in lines 3, 13.
Modifier of ⲡⲁⲍⲣⲉ 'medicine.' Likely Lyc. for ⲕⲱⲃⲉ or related to the bitter/harsh register. Synonym/parallel to ⲥⲓϣⲉ in earlier vocabulary.
Verbal/abstract noun on ⲟⲩⲱⲙ 'eat'; here the patient's 'consumption' of medicines.
Lyc. form of ⲥⲕⲁⲓ/ⲕⲁϩⲕⲉϩ 'scrape, abrade.' Fits the medical-surgical procedural inventory paralleling accumulated ⲕⲁⲍⲕⲍ.
Tentatively read as Lyc. nominal on ⲡⲱϫⲉ/ⲟⲩⲱϫⲉ 'split, cut.' Medical incision/surgery in the parable. Confidence low; flagged for parallels.
Possibly ⲧ-prefix + ⲭⲟⲩϥ from ϫⲱϥ 'foul, defiled.' The unpleasant substance the doctor sets within the patient. Confidence low.

Lycopolitan vowel-variant of ⲛⲁⲃⲉ 'sin' (in glossary). The construction 'begetting of Sin in his heart against him' is a standard Coptic moral-psychological formula. Capitalized per terminology guide.
Possessed feminine ⲡⲉⲥ- + ⲣⲟ 'gate, mouth, door.' Mercy's 'gate of going forth' = the toil and grief through which she passes out of the cosmos.
Tentatively a Lycopolitan rendering of Greek ἁπλότης. Listed among the catalogue of ascetic virtues (examination/X/continence/celibacy/anachoresis/gifts/asceticism). Confidence low; awaits parallels.
Greek ἐγκράτεια with Lyc. ⲧⲉⲣ- for ἐγκρ-. Standard monastic virtue in the elect's catalogue.
Abstract on Greek μονογενής. In Manichaean ascetic context = the celibate single life of the elect, not Christological.
Greek ἀναχώρησις. Standard monastic-eremitic withdrawal from the world.
Greek πλήρης modifying ἀναχώρησις: 'the perfect/full anchoritism.'
Tentatively read as Greek δωρεαί 'gifts' with a Coptic compound-prefix. Fits the inventory of ascetic-spiritual goods. Confidence moderate.
